templates.subtopic: Circle vocabulary
templates.source: Y8 Summer B3 Circles · S1 Circle vocabulary
templates.text: What is the name for [[k == 0|if:a straight line from the centre to the edge of a circle/]][[k == 1|if:a straight line through the centre that touches the edge twice/]][[k == 2|if:a straight line joining two points on a circle that does not pass through the centre/]][[k == 3|if:the distance around the outside of a circle/]][[k == 4|if:part of the circumference/]][[k == 5|if:a region bounded by two radii and an arc/]][[k == 6|if:the region between a chord and an arc/]][[k == 7|if:a line that touches a circle at one point/]]?

templates.subtopic: Circle vocabulary
templates.source: Y8 Summer B3 Circles · S1 Circle vocabulary
templates.text: A circle has a radius of [[r]] cm. Work out its diameter. A second circle has a diameter of [[d]] cm. Work out its radius.

templates.subtopic: Circle vocabulary
templates.source: Y8 Summer B3 Circles · S1 Circle vocabulary
templates.text: Ali says that a diameter is a chord. Is he right? Which is the longest chord? Explain.
templates.answer: Yes: a diameter joins two points on the circle, so it is a chord. It is the longest chord, with length [[2 * r]] cm when the radius is [[r]] cm

templates.subtopic: Circle vocabulary
templates.source: Y8 Summer B3 Circles · S1 Circle vocabulary
templates.text: A circle has a diameter of [[d]] cm. (a) Write down its radius. (b) A chord is [[d - c]] cm long. Is this the longest chord? Explain. (3 marks)
templates.answer: (a) [[d / 2]] cm  (b) No: the longest chord is the diameter, [[d]] cm

templates.text: A circle has a diameter of [[d]] cm and a circumference of [[d * 314 / 100]] cm. Work out the circumference ÷ diameter.

templates.subtopic: Pi as a ratio

templates.text: Use $\pi = 3.14$ to work out the circumference of a circle with diameter [[d]] cm.

templates.subtopic: Pi as a ratio
templates.source: Y8 Summer B3 Circles · S2 Pi as a ratio
templates.text: Three circles are measured: diameters [[d1]] cm, [[d2]] cm and [[d3]] cm have circumferences [[d1 * 314 / 100]] cm, [[d2 * 314 / 100]] cm and [[d3 * 314 / 100]] cm. What do you notice about circumference ÷ diameter?
templates.answer: It is always 3.14 (that is the value of $\pi$): circumference ÷ diameter is the same for every circle

templates.text: A circle has radius [[r]] cm. Mia says its circumference and its area are the same number. Is she right? Work out both in terms of $\pi$.
templates.answer: Circumference $[[2 * r]]\pi$, area $[[r * r]]\pi$: [[r == 2|if:she is right only because the radius is 2/she is not right: the numbers are different]]
